title: Renaming root node of inherited scenes disconnects the inheritance of internal scripts
body:
### Tested versions

v4.5
v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439]

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.2.0) - Single-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 (Apple7) - Apple M1 (8 threads) - 8.00 GiB memory

### Issue description

Within a scene that is created as an inherited scene, internal scripts stop inheriting changes made in the base scene if the root node is renamed.

### Steps to reproduce

Open MRP and:

1. Open Level 01 (it's a scene inheriting from "level base.tscn").
2. Find the "Checkpoint" node in the Project Tree, duplicate it a few times. (It will inherit the script from base scene as expected.) If at this point the script of any freshly duplicated Checkpoints gets modified, all other Checkpoints (including the one in the base scene) will be updated with modifications, as expected.
3. Now rename the root node of Level 01 from "base" to "L01".
4. Modify the script of any of the "Checkpoint"s created in step 2. Check which scripts are assigned to any Checkpoints except the original one. The "Path" string in the Inspector will show the original path, this is false.
5. Now close and reopen L01. Again check which scripts are associated with checkpoints. Actually it's not the script from the base file anymore! If you modify any of the newly created Checkpoints, only the Checkpoints duplicated in 2 will get affected. Any other Levels (or the base scene) will not get the modifications added in 4.

Now just to confirm this affects only the scripts, try changing the CollisionShape2D/CircleShape2D radius by dragging the handle. Any change you apply to the circle will be reflected in all other scenes as expected.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[check for inheritance.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25169380/check.for.inheritance.zip)
